translatedData.body: Hey! I understand—because the “max” limit shown on the screen can be misleading, it’s normal to scroll down to see Open Orders. Let’s clarify option 2: In Futures, the “trade fee” is independent of leverage. The fee is calculated based on the position’s notional value (trade size). So 5x only reduces the required margin; it doesn’t reduce the commission for opening a 1,000 BTC position. Example calculation: BTC price is approximately 65,500 USDT (as of 2026-07-21 00:54:51 UTC). Short notional for 1,000 BTC = 1,000 x 65,500 = 65,500,000 USDT. Commission = Notional x Fee rate. If we assume a minimum taker fee of 0.04%: 65,500,000 x 0.0004 = 26,200 USDT (opening only). If we assume a maker fee of 0.02%: 65,500,000 x 0.0002 = 13,100 USDT (opening only). When you close the position, you pay the same rate again—so the round-trip is roughly double (excluding slippage/funding). Also, since the funding fee is periodic, keeping the position open creates additional separate costs/earnings. Not financial advice; these rates can vary by VIP level, maker/taker, and promotions—please verify from your own Fee Schedule. DYOR. By the way, there is no “official token” for BiBi/Binance AI; coins released under that name could be scams.

Here's what happened when a trader went 34x long on $ETH and sat on a +24,760.13 USDT unrealized PnL.

Most traders don’t lose because they were wrong. They lose because they were right, got comfortable, and had no exit plan when leverage started doing leverage things.

The lesson isn’t that the trade was bad. It’s that unrealized profit is still market risk until it’s protected, trimmed, or closed. With high leverage, the question is rarely “am I bullish?” It’s “what happens if I’m right but price dips first?”

Russia’s national Duma today has entered a critical stage of review for its crypto market regulatory bill. The bill aims to crack down on illegal use of cryptocurrencies while providing a compliant framework for international settlements. Non-professional investors may need to pass tests, and will be subject to annual purchase limits, trading through licensed institutions, and restrictions on the scope of asset liquidity.

2. Bitcoin Miner Firms’ AI Transformation Boosts Market Sentiment
Hut 8 and IREN have disclosed large AI computing-power and cloud service contracts, lifting the share prices of related mining firms. BitMine, an Ethereum treasury company, says its ETH holdings have grown to 5.78 million coins—about 4.8% of circulating supply—nearing its goal of holding 5% ETH. South Korea’s KOSPI index year-to-date volatility has risen to a high level, even exceeding that of Bitcoin. The heavy weighting of major AI-chip stocks such as Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, combined with individual investors’ widespread use of leveraged ETFs, is amplifying market swings. Institutions warn that leveraged products may become a key risk point going forward.

After holding for so long, on July 20th I finally saw a reassuring signal.
I’ve held ETH for a long time, and there were a few times when I almost sold it.
It wasn’t because I’d lost confidence in it—it was more like that feeling of “holding on without knowing what you’re waiting for,” which really wears people down. When it’s up, it moves slowly; when it drops, it falls fast. Layer 2 has been running at full speed, while the mainnet seems to be fading into the background.
On July 20th, ETH opened at $1,871, and I saw two things that made me breathe a little easier.
First: the capital flows into and out of the ETH ETF have changed. In the past week, the BTC ETF saw small net outflows of about $84 million, but the ETH ETF actually saw net inflows of about $70.5 million. Institutions are rotating capital between BTC and ETH—money hasn’t left the crypto market; it has been shifted from BTC into ETH. This isn’t retail behavior; it’s institutions reassessing ETH’s relative value.
Second: the Devnet-5 testing for the Glamsterdam upgrade is underway, with the public testnet targeting July to August. This upgrade introduces ePBS and a parallel transaction-processing underlying architecture. This isn’t minor tinkering—it’s truly work happening at Ethereum’s base layer.
Whether holders get an explanation by the end of the year depends on whether these two developments can keep gaining momentum.
How many long-time ETH holders are still out there in the square? Has this institutional rotation made you feel anything?

【That scene from late 2018 seems to be back again】

I’ve been through a few bull-bear cycles. Saying “history repeats itself” sounds light and easy, but when you’re really on the trading floor watching it happen, the feeling is completely different.

From November to December 2018, the fear index swung between 25 and 30 for two whole months. Bitcoin just went sideways between 3,200 and 3,600. Back then, all I heard around me was, “It still has to drop another 50%.” So what happened? The market took off in the first quarter of 2019.

Now, the ETH playbook—no matter how I look at it, it feels strangely familiar. The price is stuck in the 1,800 to 1,950 range. Trading volume has expanded, but the direction still won’t commit. The fear index is 29—yes, still in the panic zone. But there’s a subtle detail: ETH has quietly risen by nearly 8% this week, while BTC’s market share is actually moving upward. What does that mean? Capital is defending ETH.

I’m not saying this is the bottom. But based on my experience, when the fear index is low and a major coin starts refusing to keep falling, it’s often a sign that a real bottom is approaching. History may not repeat in a simple way, but human nature has never changed.

As for valuation—off the high, it’s down 62%. That kind of drawdown would be catastrophic in any traditional industry. But when I decide whether an asset will turn around, I never look only at how much it has dropped. I also look at whether its fundamentals have been fundamentally damaged. DeFi is still running, staking is still being used, and the ecosystem isn’t dead—it’s just that market sentiment has thrown it into an oversold zone. At times like this, what you need to do is wait for direction to confirm.

I’m watching two key points right now: whether 1,800 can hold, and whether 1,950 can break upward with volume. Holding means there’s a chance; a breakout is the signal. I don’t need to emphasize stop-loss—if you’re alive, you have the right to talk about what comes next.

【2018年底那一幕，好像又回来了】

我经历过几轮牛熊了，"历史重演"这四个字说出来轻飘飘的，但等你真的在场子里看着的时候，感受完全不一样。

2018年11月到12月，恐惧指数在25到30之间晃了整整两个月，比特币在3200到3600横着不动。那时候我身边全是"还要再跌50%"的声音。结果呢？2019年一季度市场就起来了。

现在ETH的剧本，我怎么看怎么眼熟。价格卡在1800到1950这个区间，成交量放大了，但方向迟迟不选。恐惧指数29，没错，还在恐慌区。但这里有个很微妙的东西——ETH这一周悄悄涨了快8%，而BTC的市场占比反而在往上走。这意味着什么？资金在护ETH的盘。

我不是说这就是底。但从我的经验看，恐惧指数在低位、而某个主流币开始拒绝下跌的时候，往往是真正底部的前兆。历史不会简单重复，可人性从来没变过。

至于估值——从高点下来跌了62%，这个跌幅放在任何传统行业都是灾难级。但我判断一个资产会不会起来，从来不只是看跌了多少，而是看它的基本面有没有被根本性破坏。DeFi还在跑，质押还在用，生态没死，只是市场情绪把它砸到了超跌区间。这种时候，要做的就是等方向确认。

我现在观察两个关键点：1800能不能守住，1950能不能放量突破。守住就有戏，突破就是信号。止损这事不用我强调，活着才有资格谈以后。
